findings.summary: The site ignores the user’s dark colour preference.
findings.evidence: The dark-condition screenshot is visually identical to the light screenshot; the probe reports colorScheme "normal" and a white body background.
findings.suggestedFix: Declare color-scheme and use prefers-color-scheme or light-dark() to retint text, surfaces, controls, and browser chrome.

findings.summary: There is no explicit high-contrast or forced-colours adaptation.
findings.evidence: Under prefers-contrast: more, the probe finds no prefers-contrast/forced-colors rule and the page colours remain unchanged.
findings.suggestedFix: Add forced-colors and prefers-contrast adjustments for essential text, focus indicators, controls, and scrollbars.

findings.summary: Navigation between the site’s many server-rendered routes swaps abruptly.
findings.evidence: The DOM contains 1,177 links and no site-specific transition treatment; route changes are full documents without an @view-transition rule.
findings.suggestedFix: Add a progressive-enhancement @view-transition rule and stable view-transition-name hooks, while respecting reduced motion.

findings.summary: Very long pages provide little scroll-position guidance.
findings.evidence: Mobile layout height is 16,394px, while the screenshots show no reading/result progress indicator or scroll-state-aware persistent chrome.
findings.suggestedFix: Add lightweight scroll-state cues where useful, such as a results/date marker or article reading progress, without crowding content.

findings.summary: Repeated betting banners and a sticky bottom ad obscure and compete with core scores and article content.
findings.evidence: Mobile screenshots show duplicate 8XBET banners above primary content and a fixed banner overlaying match rows/article content near the bottom viewport edge.
findings.suggestedFix: Remove duplicate ads, reserve non-overlay slots, cap ad density, and provide a clear dismiss control for any unavoidable overlay.

findings.summary: Components rely on page-level responsive rules rather than container-aware adaptation.
findings.evidence: The computed-style probe finds zero elements establishing a container context across reused score, article, and match-card layouts.
findings.suggestedFix: Introduce container-type on reusable modules and @container rules where cards appear in main and sidebar widths; retain viewport fallbacks.

findings.summary: Keyboard focus is invisible and many interactive targets are too small.
findings.evidence: Programmatic focus on the first visible link yields outline: none and no box shadow; the probe finds many links only 14–30px tall.
findings.suggestedFix: Add a strong :focus-visible indicator and enlarge hit areas to at least 44×44 CSS px where practical without shrinking text.

findings.summary: Largest Contentful Paint misses the good threshold.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse reports LCP 3.9s and the CDP trace reports LCP/FCP 4.15s; CLS is good and TBT is low.
findings.suggestedFix: Prioritise the LCP content, reduce critical request delay, and defer below-fold ads and tracking scripts.

findings.summary: Resource delivery delays the main content and includes poorly prepared images.
findings.evidence: The HAR records 48 requests and 1.11MB transferred; image evidence finds 12 images without dimensions and 30 below-fold images not lazy-loaded.
findings.suggestedFix: Reserve image dimensions, lazy-load below-fold imagery, preload only the true LCP asset, and audit cache/render-blocking chains.

findings.summary: The page ships substantial unused CSS and JavaScript, much of it third-party tracking code.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse estimates 174KiB unused JavaScript and 30KiB unused CSS, including Google/Facebook scripts and largely unused Bootstrap/site CSS.
findings.suggestedFix: Remove unused tracker integrations, conditionally load analytics after consent, and produce route-critical CSS/JS bundles.

findings.summary: Some meaningful linked images lack accessible alternatives.
findings.evidence: The images primitive and Lighthouse both identify five result-icon images without alt text or an equivalent accessible name.
findings.suggestedFix: Give meaningful images concise alt text; use alt="" and presentational semantics only when adjacent text fully duplicates them.

findings.summary: Several navigation and ticker links fail minimum text contrast.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse reports ratios of 4.18:1 for 10px white-on-green text and 3.7:1 for green-on-light-grey ticker links, below 4.5:1.
findings.suggestedFix: Darken foreground colours or adjust surfaces and avoid 10px text so normal text reaches at least 4.5:1.

findings.summary: The document lacks a main landmark and visible keyboard focus.
findings.evidence: The probe reports only HEADER and FOOTER landmarks; Lighthouse fails landmark-one-main, and focused links have no outline or shadow.
findings.suggestedFix: Wrap primary content in <main>, keep headings logical, and add a consistent :focus-visible treatment throughout.

findings.summary: Dense small text and ads make scan-heavy score pages hard to read.
findings.evidence: Screenshots show 10–12px navigation/ticker copy, tightly packed rows, clipped long labels, and repeated banners interrupting reading.
findings.suggestedFix: Raise minimum text size/line height, allow labels to wrap safely, and increase spacing between distinct score groups.

findings.summary: Image markup and delivery have widespread hygiene problems.
findings.evidence: Of 51 images, 12 lack width/height, 22 are oversized for display, 48 use legacy formats, and five lack alt attributes.
findings.suggestedFix: Add intrinsic dimensions, generate right-sized WebP/AVIF variants with srcset/sizes, and repair alt semantics.

findings.summary: One tab control is exposed as a non-crawlable javascript: link.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse flags #button-newest with href="javascript:void(0)"; raw/rendered content is otherwise fully available and links are largely crawlable.
findings.suggestedFix: Use a <button> for in-page state changes or a real href for navigable destinations, with progressive enhancement.

findings.summary: Transport is HTTPS, but baseline security headers and cookie flags are missing.
findings.evidence: Header evidence finds no CSP, HSTS, or X-Content-Type-Options; all three analytics cookies lack Secure and two use SameSite=None with 400-day expiry.
findings.suggestedFix: Set HSTS, nosniff, and a restrictive CSP; set appropriate Secure/SameSite cookie attributes and shorten analytics retention.

findings.summary: Tracking starts across multiple third parties without an evident consent choice.
findings.evidence: The tracker probe finds seven third-party origins and Google Tag Manager, DoubleClick, and Facebook trackers; screenshots show no consent control.
findings.suggestedFix: Default to no non-essential tracking, request informed consent, minimise events and retention, and remove redundant vendors.

findings.summary: Several browser-enforced defensive policies are absent.
findings.evidence: Headers lack Referrer-Policy and Permissions-Policy as well as CSP/HSTS; X-Frame-Options SAMEORIGIN is present.
findings.suggestedFix: Add a least-privilege Permissions-Policy, strict Referrer-Policy, CSP frame-ancestors, and evaluate Trusted Types for script sinks.

findings.summary: Match times are shown without time-zone context.
findings.evidence: Global fixtures display bare times such as 23:00 and 08:00; no visible zone or user-local indicator explains which time basis applies.
findings.suggestedFix: Store instants unambiguously and render with Intl.DateTimeFormat, explicitly labelling venue or user-local time.

findings.summary: Gambling promotions dominate the primary information task and use aggressive inducement copy.
findings.evidence: Across homepage, live, article, and match views, repeated betting CTAs and claims such as “HOÀN TIỀN 100%” appear before or over core content without clear sponsored labelling.
findings.suggestedFix: Clearly label sponsored placements, remove misleading absolutes, reduce frequency, and keep betting CTAs subordinate to score/editorial content.

findings.summary: Most imagery uses legacy or oversized assets.
findings.evidence: Image evidence reports 48/51 legacy-format images, 22 oversized images, and 30 below-fold images loaded eagerly.
findings.suggestedFix: Serve right-sized WebP/AVIF, use responsive sources, lazy-load below-fold imagery, and replace animated GIF indicators with CSS/SVG where possible.

findings.summary: Background analytics work and unused code consume resources without improving the score task.
findings.evidence: Tracker evidence finds seven third-party origins; Lighthouse estimates 174KiB unused JS, led by Google and Facebook integrations.
findings.suggestedFix: Remove redundant trackers, batch essential analytics, and load non-essential work only after consent and idle time.

findings.summary: Third-party scripts and repeated animated ad media are disproportionate to the core text-and-score experience.
findings.evidence: The HAR transfers 1.11MB across 48 requests, including 497KB script and repeated animated betting banners visible on every representative mobile template.
findings.suggestedFix: Set a third-party budget, defer ads below core content, avoid duplicated animated creatives, and cache assets effectively.

Improve long-page orientation and component-level responsiveness
